# Product page: Trail Runner 2

A product page for our new trail running shoe, Trail Runner 2, on the Stride online store. The store is already a React app with a homepage that links to `/products/trail-runner-2`; build the product page at that address, using mock data, and don't add any packages to the app beyond React and its build tool. For the look, you can take inspiration from this design:

![Trail Runner 2 product page](design.jpg)

- **Store:** the shopper sees the store name and how many items are in their cart.
- **Path:** the shopper sees where the shoe sits in the store, such as Shop, Trail, Trail Runner 2, and can go back to any earlier step.
- **Photos:** the shopper sees one photo of the shoe at a time and can move to the next or previous one, going back to the first after the last.
- **Price:** the shopper sees the price and can point at a small "i" next to it to learn that it includes taxes.
- **Color:** the shopper can choose blue, black or grey; only the chosen color shows until they change it, each with a round swatch.
- **Size:** the shopper picks one size from a list that only opens when they want to change it; only the chosen size shows, and sold-out sizes can't be picked.
- **Size guide:** the shopper can open a size chart over the page from next to the size, enter their foot length and choose US or EU to get their size, and must close it to continue.
- **Quantity:** the shopper can choose how many pairs to buy, typing the number or changing it by one.
- **Add to cart:** the shopper adds the shoe to the cart and sees a confirmation; without a size they are asked to pick one.
- **Wishlist:** the shopper can save or unsave the shoe with a heart.
- **More information:** details, reviews and shipping sit side by side below everything, with one section shown at a time.
- **Questions:** a few common questions about the shoe, each with its answer hidden until the shopper opens it.
- **Bottom of the page:** the shopper finds customer help, company and social media links.

content.text: It's intermittent: 1 failure in 4 full runs, and clean in 3 more. The likely cause is a load race. `createRoot().render()` is asynchronous, so the page can reach the `load` event before React has committed any DOM. Then the first Tab focuses nothing, and `:focus` matches an empty body. I'll commit the initial render synchronously with `flushSync`, which is a reasonable change anyway because the page is never shown empty, and then run the suite repeatedly to confirm.

content.text:
The Trail Runner 2 product page is built at `/products/trail-runner-2`. All 29 existing tests pass, and the app installs, builds and starts without errors. I also loaded the page in headless Chromium and checked the main flows by keyboard and mouse, with no console errors.

**What's in place**
- **Store and path:** header with "Stride" and a cart link showing the count (updates on add to cart). Breadcrumb Shop › Trail › Trail Runner 2, with the current step marked `aria-current="page"`.
- **Photos:** one image at a time with previous/next buttons that wrap around. Each colour has its own set of four views.
- **Price:** an "i" button whose tooltip "Price includes taxes." opens on hover or focus. It closes on Escape and stays open while hovered.
- **Colour:** an APG radio group of round swatches (Blue, Black, Grey) with arrow-key support. The label shows only the chosen colour.
- **Size:** an APG select-only listbox that exists only while open. Sold-out sizes are shown struck through and can't be picked. Adding to cart without a size shows "Please select a size." and moves focus to the size control.
- **Size guide:** a modal dialog with a focus trap, Escape to close, the page made inert behind it, and focus returned to the trigger. Foot length in cm plus a US/EU choice gives a recommended size.
- **Quantity, wishlist and add to cart:** the quantity is typed or set with ±1 buttons (1–10). The heart is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`. Add to cart shows "Added to your cart: …".
- **Questions:** an APG accordion, answers hidden until opened.
- **More information:** APG tabs (Details, Reviews, Shipping) with arrow-key support. Placed after the questions and before the footer.
- **Footer:** customer help, company and social links.

**Accessibility**
- Semantic landmarks, a skip link, and a visible focus ring on every control.
- Targets are at least 36px, and the layout reflows at 320px with no horizontal scroll.
- Status messages use live regions.

**Things to know**
- **Photos are generated SVG illustrations**, not photography. The repo only had a Columbia boot as a design reference, so swap in real images when they exist.
- **Mock data** lives in `src/data/product.js`.
- **No new packages.** I didn't run an automated accessibility scanner, since that would mean adding a package, so the WCAG 2.2 AA and APG conformance comes from my own review and keyboard checks, not an audit.
- **Interpretation:** "only the chosen colour shows" is read as the label showing just the chosen colour, with all three swatches still visible. The tests require all three to be visible on load.
- **Test-flakiness fix:** one run failed the keyboard-navigation test, because React's first render could land after the browser's load event. I changed `src/main.jsx` to commit the first render synchronously. Six full runs have passed since.

The changes are uncommitted in the working tree: `src/main.jsx` is modified, and the rest is new files under `src/`.
